description: A natural-language question that tempts mixing a customer-grain metric with an order-grain metric in one query. The correct answer requires two separate queries.
nl_question: By country, how many customers have churned AND what is the total revenue?

tempting_mixed_selection.why_wrong: churned_customer_count lives on customer_profile (customer grain); total_revenue lives on order_event (order grain). Mixing them forces a join that fans out the customer-grain metric by order count — a chasm trap. The compiler must reject this.

query_1.description: Customer-grain query: churned customers by country

query_2.description: Order-grain query: total revenue by country

expected_sql_shape.comment: cross-model (view path): use_view=True (the default in run_semantic_query) compiles against the pre-joined CUSTOMER_PROFILE_SEMANTIC view. join_required=true only applies under use_view=False.

final_answer_hint: Present two separate result tables and explain that they cannot be combined in one query because the metrics have different grains (one row per customer vs one row per order).
